metadata.title: Management of Stillbirth
metadata.organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
metadata.summary: This consensus document covers the definition, frequency, risk factors, possible causes, evaluation, and prevention of stillbirth. It addresses delivery after fetal death, bereavement support, and counseling and care during pregnancies following a stillbirth. It also discusses the limits of determining a cause and the uncertainty surrounding some preventive interventions.

target_population: Patients with a history of stillbirth in a subsequent pregnancy

toxicities.event: Maternal infectious morbidity after labor induction

toxicities.incidence: A population-based case–control study of 611 stillbirths reported two cases of uterine rupture among 45 women with a history of cesarean delivery who underwent induction of labor.
prevention: For fetal demise after 28 weeks of gestation in women with a previous hysterotomy, use standard obstetric protocols for trial of labor after cesarean rather than misoprostol.
For women at increased risk of uterine rupture who choose induction, ensure they understand the increased risk and remain attentive to signs and symptoms of rupture throughout labor.
toxicities.dose_modifications: For women with a previous uterine scar and fetal demise between 24 weeks and 28 weeks of gestation, the guide notes that lower misoprostol doses (200 micrograms per dose) may be preferred; further research is needed on safety and optimal dosing.

toxicities.event: Iatrogenic prematurity following abnormal, equivocal, or false-positive antenatal testing
toxicities.incidence: Delivery after abnormal or equivocal testing occurred in 16.3% at or before 39 weeks of gestation and 1% before 36 weeks of gestation. The authors of one study estimated a 1.5% rate of iatrogenic prematurity from intervention following false-positive antenatal testing before 37 weeks of gestation.
prevention: Consider the potential morbidity and cost of surveillance when deciding when to begin testing after a previous stillbirth.

toxicities.event: Neonatal complications associated with early delivery
toxicities.incidence: The excess infant mortality risk associated with late preterm birth is 8.8 per 1,000 live births at 32–33 weeks of gestation and 3 per 1,000 at 34–36 weeks of gestation.
recognition: Respiratory complications and other neonatal morbidities requiring admission to neonatal special care units are more likely with delivery before 39 weeks of gestation.
prevention: Balance the maternal and newborn risks of early term delivery against the risks of continuing the pregnancy.
If severe anxiety after a previous stillbirth leads to a preference for delivery at 37 0/7 weeks to 38 6/7 weeks, incorporate the increased neonatal risks into the decision.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Encourage cessation of smoking to reduce a modifiable risk associated with stillbirth.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women planning another pregnancy after stillbirth who smoke

prophylaxis.recommendation: Address weight loss before pregnancy as part of care following a stillbirth.
prophylaxis.target_population: Obese women with a previous stillbirth

prophylaxis.recommendation: Encourage optimization of glycemic control when diabetes is a modifiable contributor to stillbirth risk.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women with diabetes and a history of stillbirth

prophylaxis.recommendation: Recommend surveillance once or twice weekly beginning at 32 0/7 weeks or 1–2 weeks before the gestational age of the previous stillbirth. If the earlier stillbirth occurred before 32 0/7 weeks of gestation, individualized timing may be considered.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients with a previous stillbirth at or after 32 0/7 weeks; individualized timing applies after a stillbirth before 32 0/7 weeks of gestation

prophylaxis.recommendation: Recommend induction after 42 0/7 weeks of gestation for a late-term or postterm pregnancy; induction can be considered at or after 41 weeks 0/7 days of gestation.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women with late-term or postterm pregnancies

prophylaxis.recommendation: Plan delivery at 39 0/7 weeks of gestation unless other maternal or fetal conditions dictate a different time.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women in a subsequent pregnancy after stillbirth

therapies_index.name: misoprostol
approved_indications: Induction after stillbirth before 28 weeks of gestation; vaginal administration appears to be the most efficient approach regardless of cervical Bishop score.
Medical management of a nonviable pregnancy before 24 weeks of gestation in patients with a previous uterine scar is supported by randomized-trial evidence.
therapies_index.administration: Before 28 weeks of gestation, a typical regimen is 400–600 micrograms vaginally every 3–6 hours; doses less than 400 micrograms have lower efficacy. Studies in patients with a previous uterine scar and stillbirth between 24 and 28 weeks used 400 micrograms every 6 hours; between 24 weeks and 28 weeks, 200 micrograms per dose may be preferred, although further research is needed. After 28 weeks of gestation, patients with a previous hysterotomy should follow standard induction protocols rather than receive misoprostol.

therapies_index.name: mifepristone
approved_indications: When available, it may be added to misoprostol for induction after stillbirth. Compared with misoprostol alone, it shortens the time to delivery but does not appear to improve overall induction efficacy.
therapies_index.administration: Either 200 or 600 mg orally, administered 24–48 hours before induction with misoprostol when available.

therapies_index.name: mifepristone plus misoprostol
approved_indications: Management of pregnancy loss before 20 weeks; the guide describes high-quality evidence favoring the combination over misoprostol alone.
Induction after stillbirth, with more limited data on adjunctive mifepristone for pregnancy loss from 24–28 weeks.
therapies_index.administration: When available, give mifepristone, either 200 or 600 mg orally, 24–48 hours before starting misoprostol.

therapies_index.name: oxytocin
approved_indications: A high-dose infusion is an acceptable alternative for induction after stillbirth before 28 weeks of gestation.
therapies_index.administration: High-dose infusion; the guide does not specify a dose.

therapies_index.name: induction of labor
approved_indications: Delivery after stillbirth; choice of method depends on gestational age, obstetric history and patient preference.
Delivery for late-term or postterm pregnancy is recommended after 42 0/7 weeks of gestation and may be considered at or after 41 weeks 0/7 days of gestation.
After fetal demise, induction is generally preferred to cesarean delivery, although a previous hysterotomy changes management.
therapies_index.administration: Before 28 weeks of gestation, vaginal misoprostol appears most efficient, while high-dose oxytocin infusion is acceptable. After 28 weeks, use usual obstetric induction protocols. After 28 weeks with a previous hysterotomy, use standard protocols for trial of labor after cesarean rather than misoprostol. The guide calls for shared decision making and consideration of local expertise.
key_toxicities: For fetal demise between 14 weeks and 24 weeks of gestation, induction was associated with more maternal morbidity, predominantly infection requiring intravenous antibiotics, than surgical uterine evacuation.
Early in the second trimester, induction carries a high risk of subsequently needing dilation and curettage to remove the placenta.
Between 13 weeks and 24 weeks of gestation, induction had higher complication rates than dilation and evacuation in a cited study.
Uterine rupture is a concern in patients with a previous hysterotomy; a cited study reported two cases among women with a cesarean history who underwent induction.
monitoring: During induction in patients at increased risk of uterine rupture, remain alert for signs and symptoms of rupture throughout labor.

therapies_index.name: dilation and evacuation
approved_indications: An option for delivery after stillbirth. In the second trimester, it can be offered when an experienced health care provider is available.
therapies_index.administration: Requires an experienced health care provider when offered in the second trimester. Counseling should explain that the procedure may reduce the usefulness of autopsy for identifying visible fetal abnormalities and often prevents seeing or holding the fetus afterward.

therapies_index.name: dilation and curettage
approved_indications: Removal of the placenta when needed after induction and delivery of the fetus, particularly early in the second trimester.

therapies_index.name: cervical ripening with a transcervical Foley catheter
approved_indications: A potentially helpful addition to induction after 28 weeks of gestation in a patient with a previous hysterotomy and an unfavorable cervical examination.
therapies_index.administration: Transcervical Foley catheter for cervical ripening.

therapies_index.name: trial of labor after cesarean
approved_indications: After fetal demise beyond 28 weeks of gestation in a patient with a previous hysterotomy, induction should follow standard obstetric protocols for trial of labor after cesarean rather than use misoprostol. Limited data favor trial of labor after one previous low transverse cesarean delivery.
therapies_index.administration: Use standard obstetric protocols. Individualize the delivery plan after a previous classical cesarean delivery or multiple previous cesarean deliveries.
key_toxicities: Uterine rupture is an increased concern for patients with a history of classical hysterotomy or transfundal surgery who choose induction.
monitoring: Watch for signs and symptoms of uterine rupture throughout labor in patients at increased risk.

therapies_index.name: cesarean delivery
approved_indications: For fetal demise, it generally should be reserved for unusual circumstances because it carries potential maternal morbidity without fetal benefit.
Repeat cesarean delivery is a reasonable option when uterine rupture risk is increased, such as after classical hysterotomy or transfundal surgery.
therapies_index.administration: Individualize the delivery plan after a previous classical cesarean delivery or multiple previous cesarean deliveries according to circumstances and patient preference.
key_toxicities: Potential maternal morbidity without fetal benefit when performed for fetal demise.

therapies_index.name: antenatal surveillance
approved_indications: After a previous stillbirth at or after 32 0/7 weeks, surveillance once or twice weekly is recommended beginning at 32 0/7 weeks or 1–2 weeks before the gestational age of the previous stillbirth.
After a previous stillbirth before 32 0/7 weeks of gestation, individualized timing may be considered.
When the previous stillbirth was associated with a specific condition such as hypertension or diabetes, fetal surveillance should follow the management guidance for that condition.
therapies_index.administration: Once or twice weekly at the specified starting point after a previous stillbirth at or after 32 0/7 weeks; consider individualized timing after an earlier stillbirth.
key_toxicities: Abnormal or equivocal results can lead to intervention and iatrogenic prematurity; these potential harms and costs should be considered.

therapies_index.name: fetal kick counting
therapies_index.administration: The guide finds insufficient data for a specific recommendation on counting kicks. It describes encouraging awareness of fetal movement patterns, responding systematically to reports of reduced movement, and using shared decision making about interventions.

therapies_index.name: smoking cessation
approved_indications: Reduction of a modifiable stillbirth risk before a subsequent pregnancy after stillbirth.
therapies_index.administration: Included in prepregnancy or initial prenatal care after stillbirth.

therapies_index.name: weight loss
approved_indications: A prepregnancy measure for women with obesity who have had a stillbirth.

therapies_index.name: glycemic control
approved_indications: In diabetes, strict control before pregnancy aiming for HgbA1C less than 7%, with maternal euglycemia maintained during pregnancy, may reduce stillbirth risk.
Optimization of glycemic control is an example of addressing a modifiable risk in a pregnancy after stillbirth.
therapies_index.administration: Aim for HgbA1C less than 7% before pregnancy and maintain maternal euglycemia during pregnancy.
monitoring: HgbA1C before pregnancy and maternal glycemic status during pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: bereavement care
approved_indications: Support for parents and families after stillbirth, individualized to their personal, cultural and religious needs.
therapies_index.administration: Provide emotional and practical support, clear communication, shared decision making and timely explanation of test results. Referral to a bereavement counselor, peer support group or mental health professional may be advisable for grief and depression.

recommendations.statement: Do not include testing for inherited thrombophilias in a stillbirth evaluation.
recommendations.rationale: Inherited thrombophilias have not been associated with stillbirth.

recommendations.statement: If a woman declines invasive testing, genetic analysis may use a placental sample, an umbilical cord segment, or internal fetal tissue.
Incorporate microarray analysis into the stillbirth evaluation to improve testing success and detection of genetic abnormalities compared with conventional karyotyping.
recommendations.rationale: Microarray analysis can provide a genetic diagnosis from nonviable tissue and detect abnormalities that conventional karyotyping may miss.

recommendations.statement: Use the clinical history and identified fetal abnormalities to direct genetic testing for particular abnormalities.
Evaluate stillbirth with fetal autopsy, gross and histologic assessment of the placenta, umbilical cord, and membranes, and genetic testing.
Have a trained pathologist examine the placenta, umbilical cord, and fetal membranes both grossly and microscopically as an essential part of the stillbirth evaluation.
recommendations.rationale: This examination is the most useful individual component of the evaluation.

recommendations.statement: Examine the stillborn fetus promptly, documenting dysmorphic findings and measuring weight, length, and head circumference.

recommendations.rationale: Autopsy is among the most useful tests for identifying the cause of death.

recommendations.statement: Perform genetic analysis in every stillbirth case after obtaining appropriate parental permission.
recommendations.rationale: Genetic testing has sufficient diagnostic yield to support its use in all cases.

recommendations.statement: Include relevant history and physical findings on the laboratory requisition for cytogenetic testing.
recommendations.rationale: These details help laboratory personnel interpret the results.

recommendations.statement: Obtain a comprehensive maternal history to identify conditions, or symptoms suggesting conditions, associated with stillbirth.
When choosing a delivery method after fetal demise, weigh each strategy’s risks and benefits in the individual clinical situation, consider institutional expertise, and use shared decision making.
recommendations.context: Selection of a delivery method after fetal demise.

recommendations.statement: Communicate autopsy, placental examination, laboratory, and cytogenetic results promptly to the clinicians involved and the deceased infant’s family.
Tailor bereavement care to the parents’ individual, cultural, and religious needs.

For a previous stillbirth at or after 32 0/7 weeks, provide antenatal surveillance once or twice weekly beginning at 32 0/7 weeks or 1–2 weeks before the gestational age of the previous stillbirth. If the previous stillbirth occurred before 32 0/7 weeks of gestation, individualized timing of surveillance may be considered.

conditions.name: Stillbirth
conditions.description: The document uses stillbirth for delivery of a fetus without signs of life. Reporting criteria vary among U.S. states; the suggested threshold is 20 weeks or greater of gestation when gestational age is known, or a weight greater than or equal to 350 grams when it is unknown. U.S. vital statistics include fetal deaths at a stated or presumed gestation of 20 weeks or more. Terminations for life-limiting fetal anomalies and inductions for previable premature rupture of membranes are classified as pregnancy terminations rather than stillbirths.
conditions.epidemiology: In the United States, stillbirth occurs in 1 in 160 deliveries, with approximately 23,600 reported annually at 20 weeks or greater of gestation. The U.S. rate in 2013 was 5.96 per 1,000 live births, compared with 6.61 in 2006 and 6.05 per 1,000 births in 2012. From 2012 to 2013, the early stillbirth rate fell from 3.11 to 3.01 per 1,000 births; the late stillbirth rates of 2.96 and 2.97 per 1,000 births, respectively, did not differ significantly. Associated factors include non-Hispanic black race, nulliparity, advanced maternal age, obesity, preexisting diabetes, chronic hypertension, smoking, alcohol use, assisted reproductive technology, multiple gestation, male fetal sex, unmarried status, and adverse obstetric history. Some factors, such as smoking, are modifiable, whereas many are not. Infection is associated with approximately 10–20% of stillbirths in developed countries, placental abruption is identified as the cause in 5–10% of cases, and umbilical cord abnormalities account for approximately 10%, although a cord-related cause requires cautious assessment. A substantial proportion remains unexplained after thorough evaluation.
conditions.clinical_presentation: At delivery, breathing, heartbeats, umbilical cord pulsation, and definite voluntary muscle movements are absent. Examination may identify dysmorphic features, inconsistent growth measurements, anomalies, hydrops, or growth restriction; these findings can increase the diagnostic yield of fetal autopsy and genetic analysis.

subtypes.name: late stillbirth
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Occurs at 28 weeks or greater of gestation.

subtypes.name: unexplained stillbirth
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A definite cause cannot be assigned despite evaluation.

subtypes.name: antepartum stillbirth
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Identified separately in the document's analysis of genetic diagnostic yield.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate the cause of death, developmental abnormalities, growth, and evidence of infection.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Offer during stillbirth evaluation; obtain appropriate parental permission. Diagnostic yield is greater when dysmorphic features, inconsistent growth measurements, anomalies, hydrops, or growth restriction are present.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: In a study of 512 fully evaluated stillbirths, autopsy was considered useful for establishing a cause in 42.4% (95% CI, 36.9–48.4).

diagnostic_workup.test: gross and histologic examination of the placenta, umbilical cord, and membranes
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess placental disease, infection, genetic abnormalities, anemia, abruption, cord thrombosis, velamentous insertion, and vasa previa.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Essential to stillbirth evaluation; a trained pathologist should perform the examination. In multifetal gestations, establish chorionicity and identify vascular anastomoses.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: In a study of 512 fully evaluated stillbirths, placental pathology was considered useful for establishing a cause in 64.6% (95% CI, 57.9–72.0). Knots or entanglement alone do not establish a cord-related cause of death.

diagnostic_workup.test: prompt general examination of the stillborn fetus
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Document dysmorphic findings and measure weight, length, and head circumference.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As soon as possible after delivery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Foot length can be especially useful for estimating gestational age before 23 weeks of gestation.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Preserve whole-body, facial, extremity, palm, and abnormality-specific findings for later specialist review.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During fetal examination, particularly when a geneticist is unavailable locally.

diagnostic_workup.test: partial autopsy or external examination by a trained pathologist
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Provide an alternative assessment when a complete autopsy is unacceptable to the family.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: If the family declines complete autopsy.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Provide alternatives or adjuncts to examination when complete autopsy is declined.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: If the family is uncomfortable with complete autopsy.

diagnostic_workup.test: wholebody X-ray with anterior–posterior and lateral views
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Look for an unrecognized skeletal abnormality or further characterize an apparent deformity.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of the stillborn fetus when skeletal findings warrant imaging.
Perform in all cases after appropriate parental permission; select evaluations for specific abnormalities according to clinical history and detected fetal abnormalities.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: In a study of 512 fully evaluated stillbirths, karyotype or microarray testing was considered useful for establishing a cause in 11.9% (95% CI, 9.1–15.3).

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect aneuploidy and copy number variants, including smaller deletions and duplications not detected by karyotype.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Preferred genetic evaluation in the stillbirth workup, subject to cost and availability.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Compared with karyotype analysis, microarray analysis increased diagnosis of a genetic cause to 41.9% in all stillbirths, 34.5% in antepartum stillbirths, and 53.8% in stillbirths with anomalies. Its ability to analyze nonviable tissue contributes to its higher diagnostic yield.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify chromosomal abnormalities and assess the fetus when a parent has a balanced chromosomal rearrangement or mosaic karyotype.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: An option when microarray is not readily available; particularly important with a parental translocation, inversion, or mosaic karyotype.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: An abnormal karyotype is found in approximately 6–13% of stillbirths. Cell culture fails in up to 50% of karyotype attempts.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Obtain a cytogenetic specimen before delivery.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Particularly valuable when delivery is not imminent.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: It has the highest yield among the specimen approaches described. In a Netherlands study, invasive testing achieved a tissue culture rate of 85%, compared with 28% for fetal tissue sampled after birth.

diagnostic_workup.test: placental block, umbilical cord segment, or internal fetal tissue specimen for cytogenetic analysis
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Provide tissue for genetic analysis when needed, including when invasive testing is declined.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: A placental block should come from below the cord insertion and include the chorionic plate; internal specimens that tolerate low-oxygen conditions include costochondral or patellar tissue.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Fetal skin is a suboptimal specimen.

diagnostic_workup.test: comparative genomic hybridization or single nucleotide probe and copy number probe microarrays
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect chromosomal abnormalities in smaller regions that traditional karyotyping can miss.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As approaches to genetic analysis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Single nucleotide probe arrays can additionally detect uniparental disomy and consanguinity.

diagnostic_workup.test: maternal medical, obstetric, exposure, and family history with a three-generation pedigree
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify conditions or symptoms associated with stillbirth and possible inherited disorders.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During maternal evaluation after stillbirth.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Relevant findings include recurrent losses, developmental delay or structural anomalies among live-born relatives, consanguinity, arrhythmias, and sudden death.

diagnostic_workup.test: review of original medical records and prenatal ultrasound findings
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Correlate gestational age, maternal examination, laboratory findings, and imaging with fetal examination.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Whenever records can be obtained.
As soon as possible after diagnosis of stillbirth because Kleihaur-Betke results can be falsely elevated after delivery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: In a study of 512 fully evaluated stillbirths, fetomaternal hemorrhage testing was considered useful for establishing a cause in 6.4% (95% CI, 4.4–9.1).

diagnostic_workup.test: lupus anticoagulant; immunoglobulin G and immunoglobulin M for anticardiolipin and b2-glycoprotein antibodies
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Recommended in many stillbirths, particularly with fetal growth restriction, severe preeclampsia, other evidence of placental insufficiency, or otherwise unexplained stillbirth.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A titer greater than 40 immunoglobulin M phospholipid or immunoglobulin G phospholipid, or greater than 99th percentile, is considered positive but requires confirmation after 12 weeks. In a study of 512 fully evaluated stillbirths, antiphospholipid antibody testing was considered useful for establishing a cause in 11.1% (95% CI, 8.4– 14.4).

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess inherited thrombophilia when supported by thromboembolic history.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Routine testing as part of stillbirth evaluation is not recommended; the evaluation table says to consider it with a personal or family history of thromboembolic disease.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The document states that inherited thrombophilias have not been associated with stillbirth.

diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Included in the maternal evaluation at the time of demise.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: In a study of 512 fully evaluated stillbirths, testing was considered useful for establishing a cause in 0.2% (95% CI, 0.0–1.1).

diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: According to the clinical circumstances.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: In a study of 512 fully evaluated stillbirths, testing was considered useful for establishing a cause in 0.4% (95% CI, 0.0–1.4).

diagnostic_workup.test: serology for toxoplasmosis, rubella, cytomegalovirus, and herpes simplex virus
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Not recommended as part of the stillbirth evaluation because benefit is unproven.
In selected cases, if it was not performed earlier in pregnancy.

diagnostic_workup.test: glucose screening (oral glucose tolerance test, hemoglobin A1C)
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In selected cases, including a large for gestational age baby.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: In a study of 512 fully evaluated stillbirths, glucose screening was considered useful for establishing a cause in 1.6% (95% CI, 0.7–3.1).

diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In cases of placental abruption or suspected drug use.

pathology_markers.expected_result: Present in the umbilical cord, chorionic plate, and stem villi.
pathology_markers.clinical_significance: These constitute the minimum histologic findings proposed for considering a cord accident; corroboration is needed before assigning it as the cause of death.

pathology_markers.marker: avascular villi or villi showing stromal karyorrhexis
pathology_markers.expected_result: A regional distribution is suggested alongside the other cord-related histologic findings.
pathology_markers.clinical_significance: Supports a probable diagnosis of cord accident.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Accounts for 31% of abnormal karyotypes found in association with stillbirth.
Accounts for 22% of abnormal karyotypes found in association with stillbirth.
Accounts for 22% of abnormal karyotypes found in association with stillbirth.
Accounts for 8% of abnormal karyotypes found in association with stillbirth.
Smaller deletions and duplications can be detected when karyotype does not identify them.
Has been associated with increased stillbirth risk but is not currently part of standard testing.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: The family and involved clinicians should receive autopsy, placental, laboratory, and cytogenetic results promptly. If fetal chromosomes were not obtained or did not grow, consultation with a genetics or maternal–fetal medicine subspecialist is advised to discuss possible parental chromosomal testing. Bereavement support should reflect the family's personal, cultural, and religious needs; referral for grief or depression support may be advisable.

conditions.name: previous stillbirth
conditions.description: A history of stillbirth affects recurrence counseling, surveillance, and planning in a subsequent pregnancy. The cause and gestational age of the earlier death, along with current maternal and fetal conditions, inform individualized care.
conditions.epidemiology: A systematic review and meta-analysis reported stillbirth in a subsequent pregnancy among 2.5% of women with a history of any stillbirth, versus 0.4% of women with a history of live birth (pooled OR, 4.83; 95% CI, 3.77–6.18). Evidence specifically addressing recurrence after an unexplained stillbirth is limited and conflicting. Two studies reported adjusted subsequent-stillbirth risks of 3.11 (95% CI, 0.72–13.50) and 1.00 (95% CI, 0.23–4.30) after a previous unexplained stillbirth. A retrospective analysis reported an adjusted risk of unexplained stillbirth after one previous stillbirth of 4.18 (95% CI, 1.36–12.89).
conditions.clinical_presentation: Patients may experience anxiety during a subsequent pregnancy and require additional support.

subtypes.name: previous unexplained stillbirth
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The earlier stillbirth had no established cause despite evaluation; evidence to guide subsequent-pregnancy management is scarce.

subtypes.name: previous stillbirth at or after 32 0/7 weeks
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The earlier gestational age informs the recommended start of once or twice weekly antenatal surveillance.

subtypes.name: previous stillbirth before 32 0/7 weeks of gestation
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The timing of antenatal surveillance may be individualized.

diagnostic_workup.test: detailed medical and obstetric history and evaluation of previous stillbirth
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the prior evaluation and estimate recurrence risk.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Before pregnancy or at the initial prenatal visit.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: An identified cause or recurring maternal or obstetric condition may permit more specific recurrence counseling.

diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Before pregnancy or at the initial prenatal visit if a family genetic condition exists.
Before pregnancy or at the initial prenatal visit.

diagnostic_workup.test: lupus anticoagulant as well as IgG and IgM for both anticardiolipin and b2-glycoprotein antibodies
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Before pregnancy or at the initial prenatal visit.
First Trimester.

diagnostic_workup.test: pregnancy-associated plasma protein A, human chorionic gonadotropin, and nuchal translucency
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: First Trimester, as an alternative to cell-free fetal DNA testing.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The document states that this screening modifies risk but does not change management.

diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: First Trimester, as an alternative to the other first-trimester screen listed.
At 18–20 weeks.

diagnostic_workup.test: genetic screening or single marker alpha fetoprotein
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Offer genetic screening if it was not done in the first trimester, or single marker alpha fetoprotein if first-trimester screening was already performed.

diagnostic_workup.test: sonographic screening for fetal growth restriction
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: After 28 weeks.

For previous stillbirth at or after 32 0/7 weeks, once or twice weekly surveillance is recommended at 32 0/7 weeks or beginning 1–2 weeks before the gestational age of the previous stillbirth. For an earlier stillbirth, individualized timing may be considered.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Testing can lead to intervention for abnormal, equivocal, or false-positive results; its potential harms and costs should be considered.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Increase awareness of fetal movement patterns.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Specific recommendations cannot be made because evidence that it prevents stillbirth is insufficient.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Reports of reduced movement warrant attentive, systematic assessment. A large randomized study of fetal movement awareness did not demonstrate a reduction in stillbirth rates and observed more inductions and hospital admissions.

follow_up.schedule: Before pregnancy or at the initial prenatal visit, review the earlier stillbirth and recurrence risk. Provide first-trimester dating and screening, a fetal anatomic survey at 18–20 weeks, growth screening after 28 weeks, and antenatal surveillance according to the gestational age of the previous stillbirth. Planned delivery is at 39 0/7 weeks of gestation unless other maternal or fetal conditions dictate otherwise. Severe anxiety may warrant consideration of delivery at 37 0/7 weeks to 38 6/7 weeks after discussion of increased neonatal risks.
recommended_tests: lupus anticoagulant as well as IgG and IgM for both anticardiolipin and b2-glycoprotein antibodies
pregnancy-associated plasma protein A, human chorionic gonadotropin, and nuchal translucency or cell-free fetal DNA testing
fetal sonographic anatomic survey at 18–20 weeks
genetic screening if not performed in the first trimester, or single marker alpha fetoprotein if first-trimester screening was performed
sonographic screening for fetal growth restriction after 28 weeks
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Support and reassurance are included throughout subsequent-pregnancy care. Counseling should address modifiable risks, but a 2018 Cochrane review found insufficient evidence to identify effective interventions that improve care after stillbirth. Delivery planning should weigh the risks of continuing pregnancy against maternal and neonatal risks of earlier delivery. Amniocentesis for fetal lung maturity generally should not guide delivery timing.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with fetal demise in the second trimester.
decision_rules: Choose the delivery method with the patient after considering gestational age, obstetric history, maternal preferences, the risks and benefits of each option, and institutional expertise.
Dilation and evacuation can be offered when an experienced clinician is available. Induction of labor is another option.
Although most patients prefer delivery without delay, delivery timing is generally not critical because coagulopathy from prolonged fetal retention is uncommon.

alternative_regimens.name: Dilation and evacuation
alternative_regimens.summary: Offer surgical evacuation when an experienced clinician is available. Counsel that it may reduce the usefulness of autopsy for identifying visible fetal abnormalities and often prevents the parents from seeing or holding the fetus afterward.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: An experienced clinician is available and the patient prefers this approach after counseling.

alternative_regimens.name: Induction of labor
alternative_regimens.summary: Offer labor induction as a delivery option. Particularly early in the second trimester, removal of the placenta after fetal delivery may require dilation and curettage.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Selected through shared decision making after discussion of maternal risks and alternatives.

supportive_care: Provide emotional support and communicate evaluation results clearly.
Tailor bereavement care to the parents’ personal, cultural, and religious needs; referral for grief or depression support may be advisable.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: For fetal demise between 14 weeks and 24 weeks, induction was associated with greater maternal morbidity, predominantly infections requiring intravenous antibiotics, than surgical uterine evacuation. Between 13 weeks and 24 weeks, induction was less effective and had more complications than dilation and evacuation in a cited study (adjusted risk ratio, 8.5; 95% CI, 3.7– 19.8).

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients undergoing induction after fetal demise before 28 weeks of gestation, without a specified previous hysterotomy.
decision_rules: Vaginal misoprostol appears to be the most efficient induction method before 28 weeks, irrespective of cervical Bishop score.
High-dose oxytocin infusion is also acceptable.
When available, mifepristone can be added before misoprostol to shorten the interval to delivery; it does not appear to improve overall induction efficacy.

recommended_regimens.name: misoprostol
recommended_regimens.summary: Based on limited evidence, typical dosing before 28 weeks is 400–600 micrograms vaginally every 3–6 hours. Doses less than 400 micrograms are less effective.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A meta-analysis of 14 randomized controlled trials reported that vaginal and oral misoprostol regimens each achieved uterine evacuation within 48 hours in 100% of second- and third-trimester stillbirths; regimens and dosing frequencies varied across trials.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Every 3–6 hours; the cited meta-analysis assessed evacuation within 48 hours.

alternative_regimens.name: high-dose oxytocin infusion
alternative_regimens.summary: An acceptable induction option before 28 weeks.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: When selected instead of vaginal misoprostol.

alternative_regimens.name: mifepristone plus misoprostol
alternative_regimens.summary: mifepristone, either 200 or 600 mg orally, may be added to misoprostol. Compared with misoprostol alone, it shortens time to delivery but does not appear to increase overall induction efficacy.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: When mifepristone is available; administer it 24–48 hours before beginning induction with misoprostol.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Evidence supporting mifepristone plus misoprostol rather than misoprostol alone is high quality for pregnancy loss before 20 weeks, whereas evidence for its adjunctive use from 24–28 weeks is more limited.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with fetal demise after 28 weeks of gestation, without a specified previous hysterotomy.
decision_rules: Manage induction according to usual obstetric protocols after 28 weeks.

recommended_regimens.name: induction of labor
recommended_regimens.summary: Use usual obstetric induction protocols after 28 weeks.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: In general, reserve cesarean delivery after fetal demise for unusual circumstances because it entails potential maternal morbidity without fetal benefit.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with a previous hysterotomy and a nonviable pregnancy before 24 weeks of gestation.
decision_rules: Induction of labor and dilation and evacuation are both options after a previous hysterotomy.
Randomized-trial evidence supports vaginal misoprostol as medical treatment for a nonviable pregnancy before 24 weeks.

recommended_regimens.name: misoprostol
recommended_regimens.summary: Vaginal administration is supported as medical treatment of a nonviable pregnancy before 24 weeks.

alternative_regimens.name: Dilation and evacuation
alternative_regimens.summary: Surgical evacuation remains an option after previous hysterotomy.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Select according to patient preference, clinical circumstances, and available expertise.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The delivery choice requires individualized discussion of benefits and risks related to the uterine scar.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with a previous uterine scar and fetal demise between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation.
decision_rules: Both induction of labor and dilation and evacuation remain available after previous hysterotomy.
Evidence is insufficient to establish the optimal safety, effectiveness, route, or dose of misoprostol for this population; a lower dose may be preferred.

alternative_regimens.name: misoprostol
alternative_regimens.summary: Studies have evaluated 400 micrograms every 6 hours after a previous uterine scar; lower doses of 200 micrograms per dose may be preferred between 24 weeks and 28 weeks.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Consider as part of individualized induction planning in a patient with a previous uterine scar.

alternative_regimens.name: Dilation and evacuation
alternative_regimens.summary: Remains an option for delivery after previous hysterotomy.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Choose according to the patient’s preferences, clinical circumstances, and available expertise.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The document calls for further research on misoprostol effectiveness and safety, administration route, and dosing in this population.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with fetal demise after 28 weeks of gestation and a previous hysterotomy, particularly one previous low transverse cesarean delivery.
decision_rules: Use standard obstetric protocols for trial of labor after cesarean rather than misoprostol.
On limited evidence, trial of labor remains a favorable option after one previous low transverse cesarean delivery.
A transcervical Foley catheter may assist cervical ripening when the cervical examination is unfavorable.

recommended_regimens.name: induction of labor
recommended_regimens.summary: Follow standard obstetric trial-of-labor-after-cesarean protocols after 28 weeks.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a population-based case–control study of 611 stillbirths, 91% (41 of 45) of women with a history of cesarean delivery had a vaginal delivery after induction; two cases of uterine rupture occurred.

alternative_regimens.name: transcervical Foley catheter
alternative_regimens.summary: May be used to assist cervical ripening; reported uterine rupture rates were comparable to those with spontaneous labor.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: After 28 weeks in a patient with previous hysterotomy and an unfavorable cervical examination.

not_recommended.name: misoprostol
not_recommended.reason: After 28 weeks with previous hysterotomy, the document directs induction under standard trial-of-labor-after-cesarean protocols instead of misoprostol administration.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Cesarean delivery for fetal demise is generally reserved for unusual circumstances because of potential maternal morbidity without fetal benefit.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with fetal demise and a previous classical cesarean delivery, multiple previous cesarean deliveries, or another history conferring increased uterine rupture risk, such as transfundal surgery.
decision_rules: Individualize the delivery plan because evidence is limited for previous classical or multiple cesarean deliveries.
Repeat cesarean delivery is reasonable when uterine rupture risk is increased.
If a patient at increased rupture risk chooses induction, ensure that she understands the increased risk and remain attentive to rupture symptoms throughout labor.

alternative_regimens.name: repeat cesarean delivery
alternative_regimens.summary: A reasonable delivery option when prior uterine surgery increases rupture risk.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: For example, previous classical hysterotomy or transfundal surgery, after individualized discussion.

alternative_regimens.name: induction of labor
alternative_regimens.summary: May be chosen through an individualized decision despite increased uterine rupture risk.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The patient understands the increased risk and clinicians monitor for signs and symptoms of rupture throughout labor.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Cesarean delivery generally carries potential maternal morbidity without fetal benefit in fetal demise; the increased rupture risk can nevertheless make it reasonable in these circumstances.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with an ongoing late-term or postterm pregnancy.
decision_rules: Recommend induction of labor after 42 0/7 weeks of gestation.
Induction can be considered at or after 41 weeks 0/7 days of gestation.

recommended_regimens.name: induction of labor
recommended_regimens.summary: Induce after 42 0/7 weeks for a late-term or postterm indication.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A Cochrane review of 30 RCTs involving 12,479 women associated induction, versus expectant management, with lower risks of perinatal death and cesarean delivery.

alternative_regimens.name: induction of labor
alternative_regimens.summary: Induction may be considered earlier, at or after 41 weeks 0/7 days.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: When considering delivery before the point at which induction is recommended.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The recommendation concerns management of an ongoing pregnancy to reduce adverse perinatal outcomes, rather than delivery after confirmed fetal demise.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients planning or undergoing a pregnancy after a previous stillbirth.
decision_rules: Review the previous stillbirth evaluation, establish recurrence risk, and address modifiable risks before or during the subsequent pregnancy.
Provide surveillance and plan delivery according to the current pregnancy’s maternal and fetal conditions.
Evidence is insufficient to identify interventions that reliably improve outcomes after a previous stillbirth.

recommended_regimens.name: planned delivery
recommended_regimens.summary: Plan delivery at 39 0/7 weeks of gestation unless maternal or fetal comorbidities indicate another time.

not_recommended.name: Amniocentesis for the determination of fetal lung maturity
not_recommended.reason: It generally should not guide delivery timing.

response_assessment.method: Review detailed medical and obstetric history and the previous stillbirth workup; determine recurrence risk; perform diabetes screening and acquired thrombophilia testing with lupus anticoagulant and IgG and IgM for both anticardiolipin and b2-glycoprotein antibodies.
response_assessment.interpretation: Use the findings to inform individualized care and recurrence-risk counseling.

response_assessment.method: Dating ultrasonography; first-trimester screening with pregnancy-associated plasma protein A, human chorionic gonadotropin, and nuchal translucency, or cell-free fetal DNA testing.
response_assessment.interpretation: The first-trimester screen provides risk modification but does not change management.

response_assessment.method: Fetal sonographic anatomic survey; offer genetic screening if it was not done in the first trimester, or single marker alpha fetoprotein if first-trimester screening was completed.
Sonographic screening for fetal growth restriction.

supportive_care: Offer support and reassurance before pregnancy or at the initial visit and throughout the first, second, and third trimesters.
Encourage smoking cessation and, before pregnancy only, weight loss in women with obesity.
Encourage reduction of modifiable risks, including optimization of glycemic control when diabetes is present.
Offer genetic counseling if a familial genetic condition exists.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The risks of continuing pregnancy depend substantially on current maternal and fetal comorbidities. Delivery before 39 weeks increases neonatal respiratory and other morbidity risks and admissions to neonatal special care units.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients in a subsequent pregnancy whose previous stillbirth occurred at or after 32 0/7 weeks.
decision_rules: Recommend antenatal surveillance once or twice weekly beginning at 32 0/7 weeks or 1–2 weeks before the gestational age of the previous stillbirth.
If the prior stillbirth was associated with a condition such as hypertension or diabetes, incorporate surveillance into management recommended for that condition.

recommended_regimens.name: antenatal surveillance
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform surveillance once or twice weekly at the specified starting point after a previous stillbirth at or after 32 0/7 weeks.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Once or twice weekly from 32 0/7 weeks or from 1–2 weeks before the gestational age of the previous stillbirth.

supportive_care: Provide support and reassurance during the subsequent pregnancy.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Surveillance can result in intervention-related morbidity and cost. Reported delivery rates following abnormal or equivocal tests were 16.3% at or before 39 weeks and 1% before 36 weeks; authors of one study estimated a 1.5% rate of iatrogenic prematurity from false-positive results when testing began before 37 weeks.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients in a subsequent pregnancy whose previous stillbirth occurred before 32 0/7 weeks of gestation.
decision_rules: Individualized timing of antenatal surveillance may be considered.
Balance potential benefits against false-positive results, iatrogenic preterm delivery, and associated morbidity.

alternative_regimens.name: antenatal surveillance
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider an individually selected starting time after a previous stillbirth before 32 0/7 weeks.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Base timing on the circumstances of the prior stillbirth and the current pregnancy.

supportive_care: Provide support and reassurance during the subsequent pregnancy.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The surveillance recommendation is graded 2C Weak recommendation, low-quality evidence. The document cites excess infant mortality associated with late preterm birth of 8.8 per 1,000 live births at 32–33 weeks and 3 per 1,000 at 34–36 weeks.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with a previous stillbirth whose severe anxiety leads them to prefer early-term delivery in a subsequent pregnancy.
decision_rules: Maternal anxiety may justify delivery at 37 0/7 weeks to 38 6/7 weeks if the patient understands and accepts the associated neonatal risks.
Balance the potential benefit of avoiding continued pregnancy against maternal and newborn risks of early-term delivery.

alternative_regimens.name: early term delivery
alternative_regimens.summary: Delivery at 37 0/7 weeks to 38 6/7 weeks may be chosen to address severe anxiety about recurrent stillbirth.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The patient prefers early delivery after counseling about, and acceptance of, increased neonatal complication risks.

not_recommended.name: Amniocentesis for the determination of fetal lung maturity
not_recommended.reason: It generally should not determine when delivery occurs.

supportive_care: Provide additional support for anxiety associated with the previous stillbirth.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Delivery before 39 weeks is associated with more neonatal respiratory and other morbidity and more admissions to neonatal special care units. The decision also depends on all current maternal and fetal conditions.

special_populations.considerations: The reported stillbirth rate is 10.53 deaths per 1,000 live births and stillbirths, more than twice the rate in other racial groups. The disparity persists despite adequate prenatal care. Diabetes mellitus, hypertension, placental abruption, and premature rupture of membranes have been implicated, while the contributions of care disparities, environmental stressors, bias, and racism require further characterization.

Twin pregnancies have approximately 2.5 times the stillbirth rate of singleton pregnancies (14.07 versus 5.65 per 1,000 live births and stillbirths). Risk rises with gestational age and is significantly higher in monochorionic than dichorionic twins. The reported rate for triplets and higher-order multiples is 30.53 per 1,000 live births and stillbirths.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: When examining the placenta after a stillbirth in a multifetal pregnancy, establish chorionicity and identify vascular anastomoses.

special_populations.considerations: A previous stillbirth increases risk in a subsequent pregnancy, although recurrence estimates, particularly after an unexplained stillbirth, are limited. Counseling may require additional support because the cause of the earlier loss can remain unknown. A 2018 Cochrane review found insufficient evidence to identify effective interventions for improving care after stillbirth.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Review the previous evaluation, assess recurrence risk and modifiable factors, and provide support. For a previous stillbirth at or after 32 0/7 weeks, once- or twice-weekly antenatal surveillance is recommended from 32 0/7 weeks or 1–2 weeks before the gestational age of the earlier loss. If the loss occurred before 32 0/7 weeks, surveillance timing may be individualized. Planned delivery is at 39 0/7 weeks unless maternal or fetal conditions indicate otherwise; severe anxiety may justify delivery at 37 0/7 weeks to 38 6/7 weeks after discussion of neonatal risks.

special_populations.considerations: Pregestational and gestational diabetes are associated with an almost twofold to fivefold increase in stillbirth risk in population-based studies. Pregestational diabetes combined with obesity appears to have a stronger effect than either factor alone. Strict prepregnancy glycemic control targeting HgbA1C less than 7% and maintenance of euglycemia during pregnancy may reduce risk.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: After a previous stillbirth associated with diabetes, fetal surveillance should follow the recommended management guidance for that condition.

special_populations.considerations: Reported perinatal mortality is 2–4 times that of the general population. Whether strict blood pressure control reduces stillbirth risk is unknown, and the blood pressure threshold for antihypertensive treatment during pregnancy remains debated. Coexisting pregestational diabetes has been associated with still higher risk.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: After a previous stillbirth associated with hypertension, fetal surveillance should follow the recommended management guidance for that condition.

special_populations.population: Women at the extremes of maternal age
special_populations.considerations: Maternal age less than 15 years or greater than 35 years is an independent stillbirth risk factor. Risk among older women is elevated in both nulliparous and multiparous pregnancies, with an apparent interaction between first birth and increasing age. Teenagers younger than 15 years have a reported rate of 15.88 per 1,000 live births, compared with 5.34 per 1,000 live births at ages 25–29 years.

Prepregnancy BMI of 30 or greater is associated with increased stillbirth risk, independently of smoking, gestational diabetes, and preeclampsia. Excessive weight gain is associated with higher risk among women with obesity or morbid obesity; the optimal BMI for minimizing risk remains unknown.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: For a pregnancy following stillbirth, weight loss is included in prepregnancy planning for women with obesity, but not as a pregnancy intervention.

special_populations.population: Women who smoke or use illicit drugs
special_populations.considerations: Maternal smoking and cocaine, methamphetamine, or other illicit drug use contribute to placental abruption and stillbirth. Secondhand smoke exposure also increases risk. Smoking risk varies with exposure timing and amount; cessation between pregnancies is protective.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Smoking cessation is included in planning before or early in a pregnancy following stillbirth. A toxicology screen may be used in the stillbirth evaluation when placental abruption occurs or drug use is suspected.

special_populations.population: Women whose pregnancies follow assisted reproductive technology
special_populations.considerations: Pregnancies achieved through in vitro fertilization (IVF) appear to have a twofold to threefold increase in stillbirth risk after adjustment for age, parity, and multifetal gestation. Whether the excess risk is attributable to the procedures or unmeasured factors associated with infertility remains uncertain.

special_populations.population: Women with antiphospholipid syndrome or suspected placental insufficiency
special_populations.considerations: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is associated with stillbirth. Testing is recommended in many stillbirth evaluations, particularly with fetal growth restriction, severe preeclampsia, or other evidence of placental insufficiency. Inherited thrombophilias have not been associated with stillbirth, and routine testing for them as part of the evaluation is not recommended.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Evaluate lupus anticoagulant and immunoglobulin G and immunoglobulin M for both anticardiolipin and b2-glycoprotein antibodies when testing for APS. A positive moderate-to-high phospholipid antibody titer requires confirmation after 12 weeks.

special_populations.considerations: Fetal growth restriction substantially increases stillbirth risk. The most severely affected fetuses, with weight less than the 2.5th percentile, face the greatest risk. Associated fetal or maternal conditions can further modify that risk.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: For a pregnancy after stillbirth, sonographic screening for fetal growth restriction is included after 28 weeks.

special_populations.population: Women with stillbirth in the second trimester
special_populations.considerations: Dilation and evacuation and induction of labor are options. Dilation and evacuation may limit assessment of macroscopic fetal abnormalities at autopsy and often prevents seeing or holding the fetus afterward. Induction, particularly early in the second trimester, can require dilation and curettage for placental removal.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Dilation and evacuation can be offered when an experienced clinician is available. Before 28 weeks of gestation, vaginal misoprostol appears to be the most efficient induction method; typical dosages based on limited evidence are 400–600 micrograms vaginally every 3–6 hours. High-dose oxytocin infusion is also acceptable. Mifepristone, either 200 or 600 mg orally, can be given 24–48 hours before misoprostol when available; it shortens time to delivery without appearing to increase overall induction efficacy.

special_populations.population: Women with stillbirth and a previous hysterotomy
special_populations.considerations: Both induction and dilation and evacuation remain options, but the uterine scar changes delivery planning. Evidence is limited for women with a previous classical cesarean delivery or multiple previous cesarean deliveries. Cesarean delivery for fetal demise is generally reserved for unusual circumstances because it entails potential maternal morbidity without fetal benefit.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: After 28 weeks of gestation, use standard obstetric protocols for trial of labor after cesarean rather than misoprostol. A transcervical Foley catheter may assist cervical ripening when the examination is unfavorable. Trial of labor remains a favorable option on limited data after one previous low transverse cesarean delivery. Repeat cesarean delivery is a reasonable option when uterine rupture risk is increased, such as after a classical hysterotomy or transfundal surgery; if induction is chosen, discuss the increased risk and remain alert for rupture.

special_populations.considerations: Support should reflect parents’ personal, cultural, and religious needs, including opportunities to see or hold the baby and participate in desired activities. A partner’s and family’s grief may be profound, and grief responses differ between individuals. Test results matter even when no specific cause is identified.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Provide emotional support, shared decision making, and timely, clear communication of evaluation results. Referral to a bereavement counselor, peer support group, or mental health professional may be advisable for grief or depression. If fetal chromosomes could not be assessed, further consultation with a genetics or maternal–fetal medicine subspecialist is advised to discuss whether parental chromosomal testing is needed.

artifacts.title: Principles of Bereavement Care
artifacts.source_heading: What support services and clinical counseling should be offered to the patient with a stillbirth?

rows: Adapt care to parents’ personal, cultural and religious needs, and spend time learning what they want.
Speak clearly and honestly with bereaved parents. In conversation, use “your baby or babies” rather than fetus, embryo or spontaneous abortion.
Give parents complete information about consequential decisions affecting them or their baby or babies, and enough time to weigh their options.

Acknowledge parenthood and support the creation of memories. This is thought to help parents process grief as their relationship with their baby moves from presence to memory; parents have reported regretting a lack of memories.
Acknowledging a partner’s and families’ grief
Recognize that partners and relatives may grieve as deeply as the mother; consider their support needs and make services and resources available.
Parents’ responses to grief differ in form, intensity and duration. Professionals should recognize these differences as normal rather than expect one way of grieving.
Awareness of burials, cremation, and funerals

Treat every baby respectfully regardless of gestation. If possible, discuss burial, cremation, taking the baby home, home funerals and conventional funerals before birth, allowing time to consider and arrange options. Professionals should know what is available locally.

Provide information and referrals for professional and peer support, including First Candle. Normalize and encourage seeking support; parents who use such services report feeling heard and understood and describe greater hope for the future.
Health professionals trained in bereavement care
Professionals who care for bereaved parents should seek relevant professional development and know the principles of bereavement care.
Health professionals with access to self-care
Recognize that caring for bereaved parents can affect staff emotionally, and ensure access to information on effective self-care.

artifacts.title: Management of Subsequent Pregnancy After Stillbirth
artifacts.description: Prepregnancy or initial prenatal visit: obtain detailed medical and obstetric histories; review the evaluation of the prior stillbirth and determine recurrence risk; address smoking cessation and, before pregnancy only, weight loss in women with obesity; offer genetic counseling if a familial genetic condition exists; perform diabetes screening and acquired thrombophilia testing with lupus anticoagulant and IgG and IgM for both anticardiolipin and b2-glycoprotein antibodies; provide support and reassurance. First trimester: perform dating ultrasonography; offer first-trimester screening with pregnancy-associated plasma protein A, human chorionic gonadotropin and nuchal translucency, or cell-free fetal DNA testing; provide support and reassurance. The indicated first-trimester screen modifies risk assessment but does not change management. Second trimester: perform a fetal sonographic anatomic survey at 18–20 weeks; offer genetic screening if it was not performed in the first trimester, or single marker alpha fetoprotein if first-trimester screening was already performed; provide support and reassurance. Third trimester: screen by ultrasound for fetal growth restriction after 28 weeks; begin antepartum fetal surveillance at 32 weeks of gestation or 1–2 weeks before the gestational age of the previous stillbirth; provide support and reassurance. Delivery: plan delivery at 39 0/7 weeks of gestation unless maternal or fetal comorbid conditions dictate otherwise. If severe anxiety leads to a preference for early-term delivery at 37 0/7 weeks to 38 6/7 weeks to prevent recurrence, incorporate the increased neonatal complication risks relative to the potential benefit into that decision.
